term: "Epoch"

## Simple explanation

An epoch is one complete pass through the training dataset. Training
usually takes multiple epochs, with the model parameters updated many
times during each pass.

## Technical explanation

When training uses mini-batches, an epoch consists of processing each
training example once, subject to the data loader's sampling and
drop-last rules. The number of optimizer steps per epoch is approximately
$\lceil N/B\rceil$ for $N$ examples and batch size $B$ when the final
partial batch is retained.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Epoch counts help describe training duration, but are not comparable
across different dataset sizes, batch sizes, sampling strategies, or
distributed setups. Validation frequency and compute budget are often
more useful operational measures.

## How it works

The training pipeline iterates over batches drawn from the training set.
After the final batch is processed, one epoch is complete. Data may be
reshuffled before the next epoch, and training can stop based on a fixed
budget or validation behaviour.

## Practical example

If a dataset has 1,000 examples and the batch size is 100, a full epoch
has 10 batches when all examples are used. Training for five epochs
processes five passes through those examples.

## Common misconceptions

- One epoch is not one parameter update; it usually contains many updates.
- More epochs do not always improve generalization.
- An epoch count alone does not specify how much training compute was
  used.
